mainTopic: The source and duration of ניסוך המים, identifying the תנאים behind rulings on mentioning rain, and why mentioning טל and רוחות is optional
overview: The גמרא first explains why רבי עקיבא, who uses רבי יהודה בן בתירה's hint, still starts the extra libation on the sixth day of סוכות. It then brings רבי נתן's ברייתא, which learns ניסוך המים from the uneven doubling הסך נסך: one libation of water and one of wine. Next it asks who wrote the משנה that says the water libation lasts all seven days. A first answer combines רבי יהודה בן בתירה with רבי יהודה to count days two through eight. That answer is knocked down, and the גמרא concludes that the משנה follows רבי יהושע, with the seven days coming from a הלכה למשה מסיני. The גמרא then asks which רבי יהושע and which בן בתירה are quoted in two ברייתות saying that only the מוסף leader on שמיני עצרת mentions rain. רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that both are רבי יהושע בן בתירה, called by different names before and after his סמיכה. Finally, a ברייתא teaches that mentioning טל and רוחות is optional because they are never withheld. The proof from אליהו and אחאב begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If רבי עקיבא uses רבי יהודה בן בתירה's hint, why not his ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי עקיבא. If he relies on the same extra letters as רבי יהודה בן בתירה, he should also start mentioning rain on the same day.
steps.simpleTranslation: If רבי עקיבא agrees with רבי יהודה בן בתירה about the extra letters, let him rule like him too and start mentioning rain from the second day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי עקיבא's position. It says he seems to borrow רבי יהודה בן בתירה's source without accepting his conclusion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירה learns ניסוך המים from extra letters (מ, י, ם) that begin on the second day of סוכות. So he starts mentioning rain from the second day. If רבי עקיבא also needs those letters to know the extra libation is water, why does he start only from the sixth day?

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who derives the water libation from extra letters starting on day two

phrases.aramaic: אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה —
phrases.english: If he holds like Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira
phrases.notes: 'He' means רבי עקיבא, who was discussed on the previous amud.

phrases.english: let him say (rule) like him!
phrases.notes: That is, start mentioning rain from the second day.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי סָבַר לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה נֵימָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion (on the previous amud) of רבי עקיבא's source
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's choice of the sixth day
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both opinions share the same source, they should reach the same practical ruling.

steps.title: For רבי עקיבא, the extra libation is written on the sixth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא holds that the main source for a second libation is the plural word on the sixth day. So that is where the water libation begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא holds that where the Torah writes an extra libation, it is written on the sixth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. For רבי עקיבא, the extra libation itself is anchored on the sixth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי עקיבא, the plural word ונסכיה (its libations) on the sixth day is what teaches a second libation. The extra letters only tell us that this second libation is water and not wine. So the two opinions use the letters differently, and רבי עקיבא starts on the sixth day.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva holds:
when the extra libation is written,
it is on the sixth day that it is written.
phrases.notes: This refers to the plural word ונסכיה in the sixth day's passage.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָסָבַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 1
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes how the two תנאים use the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The questioner thought רבי עקיבא depended on the extra letters, which begin on day two.
steps.terutzMaskana: The second libation comes from the sixth day's plural word. The letters only identify it as water.

steps.title: רבי נתן: the verse speaks of two libations, water and wine
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings רבי נתן's source for ניסוך המים. The double expression הסך נסך points to two libations.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא teaches that רבי נתן says: 'In the holy place pour a libation of strong drink to ה׳.' The verse is speaking about two libations, one of water and one of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא, that finds ניסוך המים in a different verse. This opens a short side discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah repeats the root of 'pour' twice: הסך and נסך. רבי נתן reads this as two separate libations. One is wine and the other is water.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Natan says:
"In the holy place pour a libation of strong drink to the Lord"
the verse is speaking of two libations:
one is the water libation
and one is the wine libation.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings an additional source for ניסוך המים
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The doubled phrase הסך נסך teaches two libations, one of water and one of wine.

steps.title: Why not say both libations are wine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the two libations cannot both be wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that both are of wine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי נתן's reading. The doubled phrase could simply mean two wine libations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse itself mentions 'strong drink', which means wine. So the doubling does not obviously point to water. Maybe both libations are wine.

phrases.english: Say both are of wine!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא תַּרְוַיְיהוּ דְּחַמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי נתן's reading
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that one of the libations is water
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A doubled word shows there are two libations, but not that they are different kinds.

steps.title: The mismatched forms show two different libations
steps.stepSummary: If both were wine, the Torah would have used matching forms. The mismatched הסך נסך shows the two libations are different, one water and one wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the verse should have written either 'הַסֵּךְ הֶסֶךְ' or 'נַסֵּךְ נֶסֶךְ'. Why does it write 'הַסֵּךְ נֶסֶךְ'? Learn from this: one is water and one is wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the uneven wording of the verse proves the two libations are different kinds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two of the same thing would be written with matching forms: both with ה or both with נ. The Torah instead mixes them, הסך with ה and נסך with נ. That difference hints at two different liquids, water and wine.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write
either 'hassekh hessekh' or 'nassekh nesekh',
phrases.notes: Matching forms would mean two of the same kind.

phrases.english: what is 'hassekh nesekh'?
Learn from this:
one is of water and one is of wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 4
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the verse's wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The doubled word might mean two wine libations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The mismatched forms show two different liquids, water and wine.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי נתן learns ניסוך המים from the uneven doubling הסך נסך. Matching forms would mean two of the same, so different forms mean two different libations.

steps.title: Who wrote the משנה that water is poured all seven days?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא wrote the משנה that ניסוך המים is done all seven days. Each known opinion gives a different number of days.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what we learned in a משנה: 'The water libation is all seven days.' Whose view is that? If רבי יהושע, say one day. If רבי עקיבא, two days. If רבי יהודה בן בתירה, six days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the main topic. It challenges all the opinions with a משנה that says the water libation lasts seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each opinion gives a different count. רבי יהושע ties the water libation only to the eighth day, so one day. רבי עקיבא starts from the sixth day, so the sixth and seventh, two days. רבי יהודה בן בתירה starts from the second day, so days two through seven, six days. None of these equals seven.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we learned in a משנה
The תנא who ties the libation to the eighth day only

phrases.english: But that which we learned:
'The water libation is all seven days',
whose view is it?

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ — נֵימָא חַד יוֹמָא,
phrases.english: If Rabbi Yehoshua, let it say one day;
if Rabbi Akiva, two days;

phrases.aramaic: אִי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה — שִׁיתָּא יוֹמֵי!
phrases.english: if Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, six days!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, הָא דִּתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי נתן side discussion and returns to the main dispute
steps.kashyaTarget: All three opinions about the source of ניסוך המים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's count of seven days fits none of the opinions' counts.

steps.title: It is רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who also counts the eighth day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, who agrees with רבי יהודה that water is poured on the eighth day too. He drops the first day and adds the eighth, which makes seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, it is רבי יהודה בן בתירה, and he holds like רבי יהודה in a משנה. As we learned: רבי יהודה says, he would pour with a לוג measure all eight days. And רבי יהודה בן בתירה removes the first day and adds the eighth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, combined with רבי יהודה's view that the libation continues on the eighth day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that the water libation is done all eight days, including שמיני עצרת. רבי יהודה בן בתירה accepts that the eighth day counts. But his source only starts from day two, so he drops the first day. Days two through eight make exactly seven.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure (here, the vessel used for pouring)

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'seven days' does NOT mean days one through seven of סוכות. It means days two through eight.
steps.whatToRemember: This is only a first attempt. It reads the משנה's 'seven days' as days 2–8, following רבי יהודה בן בתירה plus רבי יהודה's inclusion of the eighth day. Step 8 knocks it down, and step 9 gives the final answer.
steps.whyThisMatters: It is a serious attempt to fit the משנה to the opinions based on hints in the פסוקים. When it fails in step 8, the גמרא has to turn to tradition instead (step 9).

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה הִיא,
phrases.english: Actually, it is Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
and he holds like Rabbi Yehuda of the Mishnah.
As we learned: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He would pour with a log-measure all eight days.
And he (Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira) removes the first day and includes the eighth.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם רַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 6
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributes the משנה to one תנא who also holds part of another תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה בן בתירה counts only days two through seven, which is six.
steps.terutzMaskana: He includes the eighth day like רבי יהודה, so days two through eight make seven.

steps.title: Why drop day one but keep day eight?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the previous answer. If day one is left out because the hint for water starts on day two, day eight should be left out too, because the hint for water ends on day seven.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first day, that water is not poured on it? Is it because the hint for water in the פסוקים starts on the second day? Then the eighth day should be left out too, because the hint for water ends on the seventh day!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is challenging the answer from step 7. That answer said the משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The hint for water is the letters מ־י־ם, spread across the פסוקים of the second, sixth, and seventh days. Those days are the only source for water. So the hint gives a range of day two through day seven. If that range is the reason to drop day one, it should also be the reason to drop day eight. Keeping one day and dropping the other is not consistent.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? It asks why two cases are treated differently.
Hinted or alluded to (in the פסוק)
The eighth day, which is שמיני עצרת

phrases.english: And what is different about the first day, that [water is] not [poured]?
Because when water is hinted,
it is on the second day that it is hinted?
phrases.notes: The מ of מים comes from ונסכיהם on day two.

phrases.english: Then the eighth day too [should be left out],
because when water is hinted,
it is on the seventh day that it is hinted!
phrases.notes: The ם of מים comes from כמשפטם on day seven.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאי שְׁנָא רִאשׁוֹן דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה בן בתירה drops day one and adds day eight
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Inconsistency: the same reasoning (the hint covers only days two to seven) that drops day one should also drop day eight.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, based on tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the previous answer. It says the משנה follows רבי יהושע, and that the seven days of ניסוך המים come from a received tradition, not from a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה follows רבי יהושע. The pouring of water all seven days is a law that was learned by tradition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer to the question of step 6. It names a different תנא for the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא means the old answer is dropped. רבי יהושע's hint in the פסוקים is not his real source for how many days water is poured. The seven days come from a law handed down from סיני. Since the number of days does not come from a hint in the פסוקים, the problem of step 8 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the old answer is dropped.
They learned it as a received law (by tradition)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יהושע ignores the פסוקים. His reading of the פסוקים has its own job, about when to start mentioning rain. The number of days for pouring water comes from tradition.

phrases.english: Rather: it is [the view of] Rabbi Yehoshua,
and the water libation all seven days
is a law they learned by tradition,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer that step 8 knocked down
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-attribution: the משנה is assigned to a different תנא, and the source changes from a hint in the פסוק to a tradition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה follows רבי יהודה בן בתירה, and the number of days comes from the hint in the פסוקים
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה follows רבי יהושע, and the seven days come from a הלכה למשה מסיני

steps.title: Proof that ניסוך המים is a הלכה למשה מסיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחוניא teaches that three laws are a הלכה למשה מסיני: the ten saplings, the willow, and ניסוך המים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי אמי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, who said it in the name of רבי נחוניא of the valley of בית חורתן: the law of ten saplings, the willow, and the pouring of water are all a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to back up the claim it just made, that ניסוך המים comes from tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 said the seven days of ניסוך המים are a received law. Here a teaching of רבי נחוניא, passed down by רבי יוחנן and רבי אמי, shows that ניסוך המים really is on the list of laws given to משה at סיני. The other two items on the list, the ten saplings and the willow, are also not written in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given orally to משה at סיני, without a written פסוק
Ten saplings: a rule that allows plowing a field that has ten young trees before שביעית
The willow used at the מזבח on סוכות

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
phrases.english: As Rabbi Ami said that Rabbi Yochanan said

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי נְחוּנְיָא אִישׁ בִּקְעַת בֵּית חוֹרְתָן:
phrases.english: in the name of Rabbi Nechunya of the valley of Beit Chortan:
ten saplings, the willow, and the water libation
are a law given to Moshe from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 9
steps.raayaObject: The claim that ניסוך המים all seven days is a received tradition
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of רבי נחוניא, passed on by רבי יוחנן and רבי אמי
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's seven days of ניסוך המים follow רבי יהושע. The source is a הלכה למשה מסיני, not a hint in the פסוקים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the hints in the פסוקים about water are not the final source for the number of days. The practice rests on tradition.

steps.title: Which prayer leader mentions rain on שמיני עצרת and פסח
steps.stepSummary: Going back to the ברייתא, רבי יהודה reports רבי יהושע's view. On שמיני עצרת, the later שליח ציבור (מוסף) mentions rain and the earlier one (שחרית) does not. On the first day of פסח, it is the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי יהושע: the one who leads the prayers on the last יום טוב of סוכות: the later leader mentions rain, and the first leader does not. On the first יום טוב of פסח: the first leader mentions rain, and the later leader does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the ברייתא it was learning earlier and quotes the next opinion in it. This opinion is about the exact prayer where we start and stop mentioning rain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ruling sets the exact prayer where the mention of rain begins and ends. On שמיני עצרת it begins at מוסף, not at שחרית. On the first day of פסח it stops after שחרית, so מוסף does not mention rain. As the next steps show, this cannot be the view of the משנה's רבי יהושע, who starts mentioning rain from the beginning of שמיני עצרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who passes before the ark, meaning the שליח ציבור

steps.confusionAlert: Here הראשון and האחרון mean the first and second prayer leaders on the same day. They do NOT mean the first and last days of the חג.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Yehoshua:
The one who passes before the ark (leads prayers)
on the last festival day of the חג (Sukkot):
the last (Musaf) leader mentions [rain]; the first (Shacharit) leader does not mention.
On the first festival day of Pesach:
the first leader mentions; the last leader does not mention.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion about ניסוך המים and returns to the ברייתא about when to mention rain
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On שמיני עצרת, the mention of rain begins at מוסף. On the first day of פסח, it ends after שחרית.

steps.title: Which רבי יהושע? Not the one in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which רבי יהושע is quoted in the ברייתא. It rejects the first option, the רבי יהושע of the משנה, because he begins mentioning rain from the start of שמיני עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which רבי יהושע is this? If you say it is the רבי יהושע of our משנה, that cannot be. He said that one mentions rain on the last יום טוב of the חג, which means from the very start of the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to identify the רבי יהושע quoted in the ברייתא from Step 11. It tests the most obvious choice first and finds a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, רבי יהושע says only the מוסף leader on שמיני עצרת mentions rain, so rain is not mentioned at night or at שחרית. But the משנה's רבי יהושע says rain is mentioned 'on the last יום טוב'. That sounds like the whole day, starting from מעריב. The two statements clash, so this cannot be the same רבי יהושע.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposal the גמרא is about to reject)
The last festival day of סוכות, meaning שמיני עצרת
Mentions (rain, with the words משיב הרוח ומוריד הגשם)

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different words here. 'Mentioning' rain (הזכרה, saying משיב הרוח) is not the same as 'asking' for rain (שאלה, saying ותן טל ומטר). This whole discussion is only about mentioning.

phrases.english: Which Rabbi Yehoshua?
If you say it is the Rabbi Yehoshua of our Mishnah,
phrases.notes: This is the first proposal, and it is about to be rejected.

phrases.english: but he said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּיוֹם טוֹב הָאַחֲרוֹן שֶׁל חַג הוּא מַזְכִּיר.
phrases.english: on the last festival day of the Chag one mentions rain.
phrases.notes: This implies the whole day, starting from the night (מעריב).

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵי רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ? אִילֵּימָא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּמַתְנִיתִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks which רבי יהושע is the source of the ruling quoted in Step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא's רבי יהושע is the רבי יהושע of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's רבי יהושע starts mentioning rain from the beginning of שמיני עצרת. The ברייתא's רבי יהושע starts only at מוסף. These cannot both come from the same person.

steps.title: Not the רבי יהושע of the earlier ברייתא either
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא's second option is the רבי יהושע of the other ברייתא. That fails too, because he says rain is mentioned from the moment the לולב is put down, which is the night of שמיני עצרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it must be the רבי יהושע of the ברייתא. But he said one mentions rain from the time the לולב is put down.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a second candidate for רבי יהושע and rejects it as well. The answer comes in step 15, after a parallel problem is raised in step 14.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The לולב is used for the last time on the seventh day of סוכות. So 'from the time it is put down' means rain is mentioned from that evening, at מעריב of שמיני עצרת. That clashes with the ruling that only the מוסף leader mentions rain. Neither known רבי יהושע fits.

keyTerms.meaning: Of the ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in it)
From the time it (the לולב) is put down

phrases.english: Rather, it is the Rabbi Yehoshua of the Baraita,
but he said: from the time it (the lulav) is put down.
phrases.notes: In other words, from the night of שמיני עצרת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ דְּבָרַיְיתָא, הָאָמַר: מִשְּׁעַת הַנָּחָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second candidate after the first was rejected, then rejects this one too.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the ברייתא's רבי יהושע is the רבי יהושע of the other ברייתא ('from the time the לולב is put down').
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Putting down the לולב happens at the end of day seven. So this view also starts mentioning rain at night, not at מוסף.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: which בן בתירה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a further difficulty. Another ברייתא gives the same 'last leader mentions' rule in the name of בן בתירה. But רבי יהודה בן בתירה starts mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות, so it cannot be him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, there is a ברייתא where רבי יהודה says in the name of בן בתירה: whoever leads the prayers on the last יום טוב of the חג, the later leader mentions rain. Which בן בתירה is this? If you say רבי יהודה בן בתירה, that cannot be, because he said rain is mentioned starting on the second day of סוכות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second, parallel identification problem. This sets up one answer that will solve both problems together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא has the same rule as Step 11 (only the מוסף leader mentions rain), but it is quoted from 'בן בתירה'. The well-known בן בתירה, רבי יהודה בן בתירה, starts mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות (see Step 1). That is much earlier than מוסף of שמיני עצרת. So we are again missing a fitting author.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who 'passes before the ark', meaning the שליח ציבור
בן בתירה, a family name shared by more than one תנא

phrases.english: And furthermore, that which was taught in a Baraita,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם בֶּן בְּתִירָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Ben Beteira:
the one who passes before the ark (leads the prayers)
on the last festival day of the Chag:
the later one mentions rain.
phrases.notes: This is the מוסף leader, the same rule as in Step 11.

phrases.english: Which Ben Beteira?
If you say Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,

phrases.aramaic: הָא אָמַר: בַּשֵּׁנִי בֶּחָג הוּא מַזְכִּיר!
phrases.english: but he said: one mentions rain on the second day of the Chag!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ, הָא דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, parallel identification problem alongside the unresolved רבי יהושע problem.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the 'בן בתירה' in this ברייתא is רבי יהודה בן בתירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה בן בתירה begins mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות. That contradicts a rule that only starts at מוסף of שמיני עצרת.

steps.title: It is רבי יהושע בן בתירה, called by two names
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק answers that both ברייתות quote רבי יהושע בן בתירה. Sometimes he is called by his own name (רבי יהושע) and sometimes by his father's name (בן בתירה). The 'בן בתירה' version is from before his סמיכה, and the 'רבי יהושע' version is from after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Let it be רבי יהושע בן בתירה. Sometimes he is called by his own name, and sometimes he is called by his father's name. This one was before he was ordained, and this one was after he was ordained.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק solves both identification problems with one answer. Both ברייתות are quoting the same third person, רבי יהושע בן בתירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'רבי יהושע' in Step 11 is not the well-known רבי יהושע of the משנה. The 'בן בתירה' in Step 14 is not רבי יהודה בן בתירה. Both refer to רבי יהושע בן בתירה, who holds that only the מוסף leader mentions rain. Before his סמיכה he was not yet called 'רבי', so people used his father's name, 'בן בתירה'. After his סמיכה he was called 'רבי יהושע'.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule that only the מוסף leader on שמיני עצרת mentions rain belongs to רבי יהושע בן בתירה. He is called 'בן בתירה' in teachings from before his סמיכה and 'רבי יהושע' in teachings from after it. So the same name in two ברייתות can point to different people, and two names can point to the same person.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three people here. רבי יהושע of the משנה is רבי יהושע בן חנניה. רבי יהודה בן בתירה starts mentioning rain on the second day of סוכות. רבי יהושע בן בתירה is the one who starts at מוסף of שמיני עצרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: The answer shows that the ruling in Step 11 is a separate, third opinion. It is not the view of the משנה's רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Let it be Rabbi Yehoshua ben Beteira,
sometimes he is called by his own name (Rabbi Yehoshua),
and sometimes he is called by his father's name (Ben Beteira).
And this (Ben Beteira) was before they ordained him,
and this (Rabbi Yehoshua) was after they ordained him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק: תְּהֵא בְּרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן בְּתִירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the difficulties of Steps 12, 13 and 14 with a single identification.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifying the author: a third תנא, called by two different names.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We assumed 'רבי יהושע' meant the רבי יהושע of the משנה or of the other ברייתא, and that 'בן בתירה' meant רבי יהודה בן בתירה. Both assumptions led to contradictions.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both ברייתות quote רבי יהושע בן בתירה. He is called 'בן בתירה' in teachings from before his סמיכה and 'רבי יהושע' in teachings from after it.

steps.title: Mentioning dew and wind is optional
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that חכמים did not require mentioning טל and רוחות in תפילה, but a person may mention them if he wants.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: about dew and winds, the Sages did not require a person to mention them. But if he wants to mention them, he may.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא. It says that mentioning dew and wind in the שמונה עשרה is not required, but it is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the topic was rain (הזכרת גשמים), and when a person must start or stop mentioning it. This ברייתא sets up a contrast: rain must be mentioned in its season, but dew and wind are optional. This raises the obvious question of why they are treated differently.

keyTerms.meaning: To mention (in the second ברכה of שמונה עשרה)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Not required' does not mean 'not allowed.' The ברייתא clearly says that a person who wants to mention dew and wind may do so.

phrases.english: It was taught: regarding dew and regarding winds,
the Sages did not obligate one to mention them.
phrases.notes: That is, in the second ברכה of שמונה עשרה (מחיה המתים).

phrases.english: But if he comes to mention them, he may mention them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנָא: בַּטַּל וּבָרוּחוֹת, לֹא חִיְּיבוּ חֲכָמִים לְהַזְכִּיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of who 'רבי יהושע' was to a new ברייתא about dew and wind.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Mentioning טל and רוחות is optional. It is not required, but it is permitted.

steps.title: Why is it optional?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason that mentioning dew and wind is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question to set up the next step: why are dew and wind different from rain?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain must be mentioned in its season, so the גמרא wants to know what makes dew and wind different. This is a request for a reason, not an attack on the ברייתא.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the rule in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why mentioning dew and wind is optional, while mentioning rain is required.

steps.title: Because dew and wind are never held back
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא answers that dew and wind are never withheld, so we are not required to mention them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא said: because they are never held back.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חנינא gives the reason. Dew and wind always come, so there is no need to require mentioning them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rain can be held back as a punishment, so we must actively mention it as ה׳'s power. Dew and wind always come, and the world could not exist without them. Mentioning them is therefore not required.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the reason

phrases.english: Rabbi Chanina said:
Because they are not withheld.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין נֶעֱצָרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Dew and wind are never withheld, so mentioning them is optional.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle, that what is never held back does not need to be mentioned, explains the rest of the sugya about טל and רוחות.

steps.title: How do we know dew is never held back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source that טל is never withheld.
steps.simpleTranslation: And dew, from where do we know that it is not held back?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants a source for רבי חנינא's claim, starting with dew. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנינא stated a fact: dew is never withheld. The גמרא now asks where in the פסוקים we see this. It does not reject his claim; it only wants it supported.

phrases.english: And dew, from where do we know that it is not withheld?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטַל מְנָלַן דְּלָא מִיעֲצַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a source for רבי חנינא's reason.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק showing that טל is never withheld.

steps.title: Proof from אליהו and אחאב: only rain was returned
steps.stepSummary: אליהו declared that there would be no טל and no מטר. Later, 'ה told him that He would return מטר, but He said nothing about טל. The גמרא asks why, and begins its answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And אליהו the Tishbite, from the settlers of Gilead, said to אחאב: As ה׳, God of Israel, lives, before whom I stand, there will be no dew or rain these years except by my word.' And it is written: 'Go, show yourself to אחאב, and I will give rain on the face of the land.' But dew He did not mention to him. What is the reason? Because...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two פסוקים from מלכים. At first both dew and rain were stopped, but later 'ה promised to return only rain. The גמרא asks why dew was not mentioned, and starts to answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If dew had really stopped, 'ה would have needed to promise to bring it back too. Since only rain is promised, this suggests that dew never truly stopped. The full answer continues on the next amud, right after the word 'מִשּׁוּם'.

keyTerms.meaning: אחאב, the wicked king of ישראל

steps.confusionAlert: The proof is not in the first פסוק, which mentions dew stopping. The proof is in what the second פסוק leaves out: dew is missing from 'ה's promise.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the scriptural basis for why mentioning טל is optional in תפילה.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And Elijah the Tishbite said,'
who was of the settlers of Gilead, to Ahab:
As the Lord, God of Israel, lives,
before whom I stand,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יִהְיֶה הַשָּׁנִים הָאֵלֶּה טַל וּמָטָר
phrases.english: there shall be no dew or rain in these years
except according to my word.'
And it is written: 'Go, show yourself to Ahab,'
'and I will give rain upon the face of the land.'
Whereas dew He did not say to him.
What is the reason? Because...
phrases.notes: The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיֹּאמֶר אֵלִיָּהוּ הַתִּשְׁבִּי מִתֹּשָׁבֵי גִלְעָד אֶל אַחְאָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source requested in step 19.
steps.raayaSupportSource: מלכים א יז:א and יח:א: 'ה promises to return מטר but makes no mention of טל.
